name: MetaAgent - Toward Self-Evolving Agent via Tool Meta-Learning
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2508.00271, cs.AI / cs.CL / cs.IR); Technical Report, 14 pages; submitted 1 Aug 2025 (v1), last revised 1 Sep 2025 (v2). Not peer-reviewed at time of writing (Semantic Scholar lists it as a CoRR/arXiv JournalArticle).
authors_affiliation: Hongjin Qian (Tommy Chien) and Zheng Liu, both at BAAI (Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence). Corresponding author: Zheng Liu. Contact emails: {chienqhj, zhengliu1026}@gmail.com.
code_url: https://github.com/qhjqhj00/MetaAgent (Apache-2.0 license; ~45 stars / 8 forks as of mid-2025; Python; built on LangGraph; includes search/cache infrastructure with Google Custom Search + Jina Reader + MySQL cache + Elasticsearch/BGE-m3 hybrid retrieval).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/qhjqhj00/MetaAgent (single-method repo, last updated Sep 2025; not a continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).
task_domain: Tool-use / web / agentic information-seeking: deep knowledge discovery with LLM agents (multi-step reasoning + dynamic tool use over web search and code execution). Spans tool-use, web browsing, and QA.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent (single central reasoning agent plus a standalone tool-router agent and an auxiliary summarization model) test-time setting for deep knowledge-discovery / information-seeking tasks. The central LLM is FROZEN (no parameter updates, no post-training); adaptation happens entirely via in-context experience accumulation and a growing in-house knowledge base. Supervision is weak/optional: self-reflection runs without ground truth; verified reflection uses ground-truth answers only when available, and in the reported experiments experience is constructed online from scratch with unilateral (lagged) reflection so the summarized experience from a task is used only for SUBSEQUENT tasks to prevent leakage. The agent starts as a 'novice' (minimal workflow: autonomous reasoning + adaptive help-seeking) and self-evolves to 'expert' through meta tool learning.
what_is_retrieved: Two retrieval streams: (1) distilled task EXPERIENCES / lessons (concise transferable texts capturing planning, tool-selection, and information-integration insights) injected into future task contexts; (2) raw browsed web content / tool-use history stored in a persistent in-house knowledge base, retrieved on demand. Per help request, the tool router also routes to external tools (web search results, code-execution outputs) which return external knowledge.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. The in-house knowledge base 𝒞 is a GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes (raw tool-use interaction history and browsed pages accumulated across episodes and tasks), retrieved via BGE-m3 hybrid search; the accumulated EXPERIENCE ℰ is likewise a growing memory injected into context. Simultaneously, live tool calls retrieve from a STATIC external corpus (the open web via Google Custom Search + Jina Reader, and code execution). So retrieval targets both the agent-written growing store and external live sources.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval for the memory/in-house tool (search_topk=10 in the repo default; BGE-m3 hybrid top-k). For the overall task objective, BrowseComp-style tasks are framed as completeness-of-constraint problems: the agent must satisfy the INTERSECTION of all task constraints (the experience lesson 'Total Constraint Compliance: never omit any clue' enforces recovering the complete minimal set of constraints), but the retrieval mechanism itself is fixed top-k rather than a learned variable-size completeness objective.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). If mapped loosely: Retrieve (retrieve experiences + memory), Reuse (inject lessons into context), Revise (self-reflection / second-attempt revision) are present; Retain (write distilled experience + raw tool history to persistent store) is present. But the work does not present a CBR case (problem-solution) abstraction; it stores distilled lessons and raw knowledge, not solution cases for analogical adaptation.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. MetaAgent does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It grounds itself in metacognitive theory (Schraw & Moshman, 1995) and 'learning-by-doing' / meta tool learning, not CBR. It realizes some CBR-adjacent mechanisms (retain-then-reuse experiences) under a different name.
retrieval_unit: Mixed granularity: (a) experience unit = a concise distilled guideline/lesson (free-text strategy or pitfall, e.g. 'Total Constraint Compliance', 'Constraint-Driven Filtering'); (b) in-house knowledge-base unit = browsed web page / raw tool-result chunk indexed for retrieval; (c) tool-call unit = web search results and code-execution outputs returned per help request. So units span guideline-rule, document/web-page, and tool-API result.
index_source: Hybrid, online/test-time-induced growing store: the in-house knowledge base 𝒞 and the experience repository ℰ are both built from scratch online from the agent's own tool-use history and reflections (the in-house tool is initialized by simulating each benchmark's tasks three times to pre-gather web content). The external web/code tools are a static live external source queried on demand. Not an offline-induced fixed corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat hybrid vector+keyword index for the in-house tool: browsed web pages are embedded with BGE-m3 and stored in Elasticsearch, retrieved via hybrid search (dense embeddings + traditional keyword search). A MySQL cache stores raw search results and page contents (metadata-keyed cache). The experience store is an appended free-text context block. No dependency graph or hierarchical category->tool topology.
retriever_type: Hybrid: dense BGE-m3 embeddings + BM25/keyword search (Elasticsearch hybrid retrieval) for the in-house knowledge base; an LLM-as-router (the tool router agent Γ) maps natural-language help requests to the appropriate external tool (web search vs code executor). Web search itself uses Google Custom Search JSON API + Jina Reader. So: dense+sparse hybrid for memory, LLM-as-router for tool selection.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The in-house retriever uses a pretrained BGE-m3 embedding model and standard Elasticsearch hybrid scoring with no task-specific training. The tool router Γ is a fixed LLM agent that matches requests to tool descriptions 𝒟 without learned weights. No contrastive, RL, or preference-based retriever training; the 'learning' in MetaAgent is in the in-context experience/memory accumulation, not in retriever parameters.
query_construction: The central agent generates a natural-language HELP REQUEST t_i describing its unmet information need (intent expressed in NL); the tool router translates this into a concrete tool action (web search query, or code snippet). For memory/in-house-tool retrieval, the (help-request-derived) query is matched against the BGE-m3/ES index. Queries are thus thought-conditioned NL intents decomposed from the reasoning trajectory rather than raw user input.
query_granularity: Step-level: queries (help requests) are issued at intermediate reasoning steps whenever the agent reaches a knowledge gap (interleaved within the trajectory y_1,t_1,k_1,...). Experience is injected at task-level (one block prepended to the input X_t at the start of each task), so two granularities: task-level experience injection + step-level tool/memory retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated: the central agent decides when to retrieve by emitting help requests upon reaching its ability limitation during step-by-step reasoning (adaptive help-seeking), not on a fixed schedule. Experience injection is one-shot at task start; tool/memory retrieval is iterative and agent-triggered within the trajectory.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: retrieval is triggered when the central reasoning agent judges it has reached the limit of its own knowledge and generates a natural-language <help> request (an LLM self-assessed knowledge-gap signal). Not token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, reflection tokens, or a separately trained complexity classifier; the trigger is the LLM's own decision to seek help.
reranking: No explicit dedicated learned reranking stage for retrieved items is described. The tool router Γ acts as a selection/filter (chooses the best tool and returns only a distilled task-relevant subset of all retrieved knowledge), and an auxiliary model summarizes web pages, which functions as content filtering/distillation rather than a cross-encoder reranker. Elasticsearch hybrid search produces ranked top-k.
retrieved_context_refinement: Distillation/compression: the tool router Γ processes all accessible information (e.g., the full set of retrieved web pages) but returns only a distilled, task-relevant subset k_i = Γ(𝒦_i) to the central agent (an auxiliary summarization model condenses crawled page content). The in-house tool 𝒞 additionally preserves the raw full knowledge to bridge the information gap left by this distillation, so the agent can revisit/cross-reference. Reason-in-documents-style filtering is performed by the router/summarizer.
tool_document_engineering: Tools are described by a configurable, extensible tool-description set 𝒟 (raw natural-language tool descriptions) consumed by the tool router agent; an ablation ('w/ tool description') feeds these descriptions directly in-context. No synthetic-query augmentation, weighted-field embeddings, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings; tool selection is done by an LLM router over the descriptions.
index_content_separation: Yes (partial). The tool router returns only a lightweight distilled subset k_i to the central agent, while the heavy raw knowledge (full browsed pages, all intermediate results) is held in the separate persistent in-house knowledge base 𝒞 and retrieved on demand — a progressive-disclosure / index-then-content separation between the distilled working context and the full backing store.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: The external tool index is a small, manually configurable/extensible set 𝒟 (two core tools: a web search tool = Google Custom Search JSON API + Jina Reader; a code executor = Python exec()), integrated via a custom HTTP API service and the LangGraph framework, not via RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling registries. The in-house knowledge base grows live (insert route adds new pages to the ES index), giving the memory store a live-synced character, but tool integration is via REST/HTTP, not a CRUD-auto-synced live tool registry or MCP.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. Retrieval/tool-routing does not explicitly model inter-tool dependencies (no dependency graph, bipartite KG, or prerequisite modeling). The central agent composes tools sequentially via successive help requests, but inter-tool dependencies are handled implicitly through reasoning, not by a dependency-aware retriever.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + experience reuse + memory grounding: distilled experiences ℰ are injected into the input sequence X_t={q,p,ℰ_{t-1}} to steer planning and tool-use; tool-call results k_i are appended into the reasoning trajectory; the in-house knowledge base 𝒞 grounds reasoning with global access to accumulated browsed content. All in-context, with FROZEN model parameters (no training signal, no latent-token injection).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan + per-step interleaved: at task start the accumulated experience is prepended to guide planning; during execution the agent interleaves autonomous reasoning steps y_i with help requests t_i (routed to tools by Γ) and incorporates returned knowledge k_i step by step (single-central-agent unified think-and-call loop, Eq. 4/10). The minimal workflow = reason -> on limitation emit NL help request -> aggregate evidence -> answer, executed iteratively within one trajectory; self-reflection can trigger a full second attempt.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-reasoning-step within a single rollout: reasoning and tool invocation are interleaved at the step level (y_t then optional tool result k_t), with help requests issued mid-trajectory whenever a knowledge gap arises. Reflection/experience operates at the per-task granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method, no case adaptation). The closest analog is execution-feedback-driven revision: self-reflection (and verified reflection) prompts the agent to reconsider and launch a corrected second attempt, and distilled lessons are reused as in-context guidance — but there is no retrieved-case adaptation step; the central LLM is frozen and only its in-context experience is updated.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface forms injected: (a) experiences as concise free-text distilled lessons/guidelines (e.g., 'Total Constraint Compliance', 'Constraint-Driven Filtering', 'Cultural Depth in Symbolism'); (b) tool results as natural-language summaries of web pages or code-execution outputs; (c) in-house-tool hits as retrieved raw/summarized web content. So distilled strategy/guideline text plus raw/summarized document text, all as natural language.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mixed: distilled, transferable strategies/guidelines (high abstraction — generalizable planning, tool-selection, and pitfall-avoidance principles abstracted via metacognitive reflection) for the experience stream; raw/summarized browsed documents (low abstraction — concrete evidence) for the in-house knowledge base. Not raw trajectories or executable skills/programs.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Multiple in-context safeguards: (1) self-reflection scrutinizes the validity and factual grounding of each reasoning step without ground truth and triggers reconsideration/second attempts when confidence is low; (2) verified reflection (when ground truth available) abstracts which strategies/tool choices succeeded or failed and what cognitive pitfalls emerged, distilling corrective lessons; (3) the tool router + auxiliary summarizer filter retrieved content into a distilled task-relevant subset (distractor filtering); (4) the in-house tool lets the agent cross-reference evidence to catch errors. No retriever-aware SFT or trained relevance classifier.
memory_type: Hybrid procedural + episodic, non-parametric: (1) an experience/procedural memory ℰ of distilled lessons (workflow/strategy knowledge) injected into context; (2) an episodic/document memory 𝒞 = a persistent in-house knowledge base of raw browsed content (BGE-m3 + Elasticsearch). No latent/parametric memory (model weights unchanged); a MySQL cache also persists raw tool outputs.
write_back: True. The system writes back both: (i) distilled experiences ℰ_t / ℰ_self after each task (Eq. 6/7), and (ii) raw tool-use history and all intermediate browsed knowledge into the persistent in-house knowledge base 𝒞 (Eq. 9, 𝒞 <- 𝒞 ∪ (𝒦_1 ∪...∪ 𝒦_T)). Both stores grow over tasks; model parameters are never written.
online_growth: True. Both the experience repository ℰ and the in-house knowledge base 𝒞 grow during deployment/test-time (experience is built online from scratch in the reported experiments; the knowledge base is initialized by simulating each benchmark's tasks three times and then keeps accumulating browsed content as tasks are solved). Becomes 'progressively richer and more informative' over time.
write_back_trigger: Reflective (after self-critique) and on-both-success-and-failure: distilled experience is written after each task via self-reflection (no ground truth) and verified reflection (compares predicted vs ground-truth answer, analyzing BOTH successes and failures). To prevent leakage, verified reflection is performed only after the answer is finalized and the resulting experience is used exclusively for SUBSEQUENT tasks (unilateral/lagged write). Raw tool knowledge is written to 𝒞 continuously per tool execution.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure: verified reflection explicitly analyzes both successes and failures, abstracting which reasoning strategies/decision frameworks contributed to success or failure, what principles governed effective tool use, and what cognitive pitfalls/errors emerged. Failures yield corrective generalizable lessons (e.g., the case study where a wrong first answer triggers a 'check all constraints' lesson and a corrected second attempt). Not success-only.
memory_evolution_update: Experience store: incremental refine/append — ℰ_t = Ω(X,Y,A*,ℰ_{t-1}) updates and accumulates distilled lessons across tasks (transformed, not purely appended verbatim; distilled into concise transferable texts that are incrementally enriched). In-house knowledge base 𝒞: append-only union of accumulated raw knowledge (with MySQL/ES caching to dedup repeated queries). No explicit forgetting/pruning mechanism described.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval and tool-selection are NOT a trained/RL-optimized policy. The retriever is off-the-shelf BGE-m3 hybrid top-k; the tool router is a fixed LLM matching requests to descriptions; help-request emission is the central LLM's in-context decision. The adaptation is via in-context experience accumulation, explicitly without changing model parameters or post-training. Contrasts with M-MDP/soft-Q learned-retrieval works.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory. The experience ℰ and in-house knowledge base 𝒞 belong to one MetaAgent instance; there is no sharing of memory/experience across multiple distinct agents or heterogeneous frameworks. (Internally there are role-separated modules — central reasoning agent, tool router agent, auxiliary summarizer — but they are part of one system, not a memory-sharing collective.)
benchmarks: GAIA (General AI Assistant; 103 questions from the text-only validation subset, 3 difficulty levels), WebWalkerQA (680 queries; Easy/Medium/Hard), BrowseComp (1,266 hard-to-find questions total; evaluated on two topics — Art and History — totaling 257 questions). Backbone: QwQ-32B (also Gemini-2.5-Flash in a separate study).
benchmark_family: Web / agentic-browsing + tool-use knowledge discovery: GAIA = tool-use + multi-step general-assistant agent benchmark; WebWalkerQA = web traversal; BrowseComp = long-horizon creative web browsing. All in the web/tool-use information-seeking family.
baselines: Four categories: (1) Direct Reasoning w/o retrieval: Qwen2.5-32B, QwQ-32B, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-671B; (2) Direct Reasoning w/ Retrieval: RAG (Qwen2.5-32B), RAG (QwQ-32B); (3) Expert-Designed Workflows: Query Planning, Iterative RAG, ReAct (Qwen2.5-32B / QwQ-32B / GPT-4o), Search-o1-32B; (4) End-to-End Trained Agents: WebThinker-32B-Base and WebThinker-32B-RL. QwQ-32B and Qwen2.5-32B are the shared backbones for most baselines.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM) for GAIA and BrowseComp; LLM equivalence accuracy (LLM-judged) for WebWalkerQA. Reported per difficulty level and as averages. (No intrinsic retrieval metrics reported.)
headline_result: With the same QwQ-32B backbone, MetaAgent reaches GAIA avg 47.6 (Level 1 61.5 / Level 2 42.3 / Level 3 25.0), WebWalkerQA avg 52.1 (Easy 55.0 / Medium 49.6 / Hard 47.9), and BrowseComp avg 7.1 (Art 7.9 / History 6.4). It outperforms all workflow baselines (e.g., Search-o1-32B GAIA 39.8, WebWalkerQA 34.1, BrowseComp 1.9) and matches/exceeds the end-to-end RL-trained WebThinker-32B-RL (GAIA 48.5, WebWalkerQA 46.5, BrowseComp 2.7), best on WebWalkerQA (52.1 vs 46.5) and BrowseComp (7.1 vs 2.7) while being within ~1 point on GAIA — all without parameter updates.
ablations: Ablation on GAIA (Figure 3) removing one component at a time: (1) w/o self reflection, (2) w/o verified reflection, (3) w/o in-house tool, (4) minimal workflow only, (5) w/ tool description (replace tool router with in-context tool descriptions). Findings: minimal workflow alone performs poorly and barely matches Search-o1; both self-reflection AND verified reflection are critical and together form the meta-tool-learning loop that substantially boosts performance; the in-house tool is essential for a global persistent view that mitigates single-pass search-and-refine information loss; replacing the router with in-context tool descriptions beats the minimal workflow but lacks the autonomous self-evolving capability. Separate study (Table 2): swapping backbone to Gemini-2.5-Flash, MetaAgent lifts GAIA from 7.8 (vanilla Gemini-2.5-Flash) to 49.5 avg, and QwQ-32B from 22.3 to 47.6, confirming backbone-agnostic gains.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (EM / LLM-equivalence accuracy) are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, completeness) are not reported separately. Component contribution is probed only via the ablation study, not via intrinsic retrieval evaluation.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer EM / equivalence accuracy). Process is examined only qualitatively via a BrowseComp case study (showing the self-reflection-driven first-attempt failure then corrected second attempt) and the component ablation; no formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-accuracy scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Core efficiency claim is no parameter updates / no large-scale post-training (vs end-to-end RL agents like WebThinker that need extensive annotated data), achieving competitive/superior accuracy by in-context evolution alone. Infrastructure uses a MySQL + Elasticsearch cache to avoid redundant external requests and improve efficiency; search_topk=10 default. BrowseComp tasks can require browsing hundreds of web pages per question (e.g., ~48 then ~53 pages across two attempts in the case study), and the in-house tool is initialized by simulating each benchmark 3 times — so wall-clock/web-call cost is substantial, but no explicit token/latency/cost numbers are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: search_topk=10 (repo default) for web and in-house cache search; max_retries=3 for re-attempts; in-house tool initialized by 3 simulation passes per benchmark. The tool router truncates/distills retrieved knowledge into a task-relevant subset before injection; distilled experience is appended as a concise text block. No explicit token-budget cap or adaptive/precision-driven k is reported.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A - this is a method paper, not a benchmark paper. (It uses existing benchmarks: GAIA 103 text-only validation Qs over 3 levels; WebWalkerQA 680 queries; BrowseComp 257 Qs from the Art and History topics of the full 1,266.)
builds_on: Test-time scaling / agentic reasoning (Snell et al. 2024; OpenAI deep research 2025); ReAct interleaved reasoning-acting (Yao et al. 2023); Search-o1 agentic search with Reason-in-Documents (Li et al. 2025a); WebThinker deep-research agent (Li et al. 2025b); RAG (Lewis et al. 2020); metacognitive theory / self-regulation (Schraw & Moshman 1995); BGE-m3 embeddings (Chen et al. 2023); LangGraph framework; QwQ-32B / Qwen2.5 backbones; Google Custom Search + Jina Reader tooling.
contrasts_with: Contrasts with (a) manually designed expert workflows / prompt-engineering agents (Search-o1, Query Planning, Iterative RAG, Mind-Map/Agentic Reasoning, generalist coding agent) — rigid, human-effort-heavy, poor cross-task adaptability; (b) end-to-end RL-trained agents (WebThinker, Search-R1, DeepResearcher, WebDancer) — need large annotated data, risk overfitting / distribution bias / catastrophic forgetting across tasks; (c) static single-pass RAG with fixed queries — lacks multi-step dynamic integration. MetaAgent instead self-evolves in-context from a minimal workflow without parameter updates.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): self-evolving / experience-augmented tool-use agents. Sits in the lineage of agentic search + tool-augmented reasoning (ReAct -> Search-o1 -> WebThinker) but distinguished by 'meta tool learning' — frozen-LLM, training-free self-evolution via metacognitive self-reflection + verified reflection (dynamic context engineering) plus an autonomously built, BGE-m3-indexed in-house knowledge base and a modular NL-help-request-to-tool router, separating reasoning from tool execution.
